children: Meta Platforms Inc. (META, Financials), the social media and digital advertising company, has agreed to a proposed settlement of up to $17 billion that will alter how kids use Instagram and Facebook.
The accord, pending a judge's approval, would resolve litigation launched by a wide coalition of state attorneys general over the impact of Meta's platforms on children and teenagers.
Under the terms of the proposed arrangement, kids would be subject to default daily usage caps and nighttime bans that parents would have to turn off.

Meta would also improve its age-assurance algorithms, which are supposed to alert users under 18 and remove youngsters under 13 who aren't allowed on the sites. Settlement payout apart, such changes matter.

Meta makes very little advertising money from teens now but young people are crucial to the future of Instagram and Facebook. The new rules could lead to reduced interaction in that cohort, and make it harder for Meta to win over younger audiences in the long run.
The settlement will also entail continuing compliance costs like independent monitoring and new means of age verification.

The bigger concern for investors is whether the tougher constraints will stay largely confined to under-age accounts or become a precedent for further regulation of social media sites. Meta has to make the upgrades to its product and age verification, and the deal needs court approval.

title: Meta Faces $17 Billion Teen Safety Settlement
